## 4. How side-effect-on-import constrains the split

- main.ts:146 `await import('./features/execution')` is the module's ONLY reference anywhere in src/. Nothing imports runCode. The entire externally visible contract is side effects, so the split has no compiler-enforced safety net — a file that stops being imported simply stops registering, silently.
- Line 296 `const initialized = requireRuntime()` runs at module evaluation and throws if the editor/tabManager/storage are unset. The module is therefore only legal after `await initializeWorkspace()` (main.ts:136). A naive split breaks this the moment any new file is statically imported from something in the early graph — e.g. adding `import { runCode } from './execution/run-code'` to run-panel.ts, stepup.ts, or a features barrel would pull the side-effecting sibling into the eager graph and throw 'IDE is not ready yet' at boot.
- src/commands/registry.ts:100-104: register() THROWS on a duplicate id. Registration must execute exactly once. Today that invariant is protected by there being one file imported from one place. Splitting into several side-effecting modules multiplies the number of files that must never be re-evaluated — and under Vite HMR, editing any of them re-runs the module and throws `Command "workspace.run" is already registered`. This is the single strongest argument for putting registration behind an explicit initializeExecution() with disposables, rather than leaving it at module top level in N files.
- Lines 297-298 capture `editor` and `tabManager` once at module scope, while runCode re-reads them through requireRuntime() at line 66. If the editor is ever recreated, the commands and both context-menu actions keep the stale instance while runCode does not. A split should pass dependencies in as arguments so this asymmetry cannot survive.
- runtime.diagnostics is assigned at main.ts:153, AFTER the import at 146. runCode reads it lazily at line 248, which is why it works. A refactor that hoists `runtime.diagnostics` to module scope — mirroring exactly what lines 296-298 already do for editor/tabManager — would silently disable run diagnostics forever, with no error.
- bindButton at 386 needs `runBtn` present in the DOM at evaluation time; createContextKey/addAction/addCommand need the concrete editor. All of that must stay ordered behind the same initialize call.
- The four editor listeners at 439-440 and 500-501 discard their disposables. There is no teardown today; the register* functions should return Disposables so a second initialization cannot double-subscribe.

=== 3. import.meta.glob CONSTRAINTS FOR ADDING BEHAVIOUR ===

The mechanism itself does not forbid functions. import.meta.glob is Vite's build-time directory scan; with eager:true each match becomes a real static import folded into the bundle. Globbing '/languages/*/client.ts' and reading module.default as an adapter object with methods works exactly as well as globbing JSON. The real constraints are these:

(a) The pattern must be a literal, statically analysable string, and it is resolved against the VITE PROJECT ROOT, not src/ (hence the leading slash in '/languages/*/config.json'). Everything must exist on disk at build time — no runtime registration, no host-app-supplied language.

(b) tsconfig.json include is ["src/**/*"]. A .ts file under languages/ would be transpiled and bundled by esbuild but NEVER type-checked by tsc --noEmit. An adapter contract placed there is unenforced. Broadening include is possible but then the server's non-TS neighbours in the same tree (languages/python/fs_guard.py, preflight.py, turtle_shim.py) sit inside the browser tsconfig's scope.

(c) eager:true means no code splitting: every adapter lands in the entry chunk. Fine for six small objects, not fine if adapters pull in parsers. eager:false gives Record<string, () => Promise<Module>>, which makes registry access ASYNC — and that is disqualifying today, because getLanguage, getAllLanguages, detectLanguageByExtension (tabs.ts:201), monacoLanguageFor (main.ts:76) and the tree/search icon lookups are all synchronous, called during render.

(d) The generic parameter is an unchecked assertion. import.meta.glob<{default: LanguageConfig}> asserts a shape nothing validates — a malformed config.json currently produces a runtime-shaped object with no error. The server is stricter (catalog.mjs:141 wraps each parse so one bad file does not empty the catalog); the client has no equivalent.

(e) Anything added as a .ts module is CLIENT-ONLY. The server is .mjs and cannot import it. Anything added to config.json is automatically shared, because the server already reads the same file from disk. That asymmetry, not the glob, is what should decide where a given fact lives.

=== 4. COULD CONFIG.JSON CARRY THE EXTRA DATA, OR DO FUNCTIONS FORCE CODE? ===

Both, split by kind — and most of the currently-hardcoded material is data, not behaviour.

Expressible as config.json fields (and should be, because the server reads the same file): the icon map (LANGUAGE_ICONS, types.ts:71); executability (executableLanguageIds, catalog.mjs:162); ANALYSED_IN_BROWSER (main.ts:122); formatter routing (LOCAL_LANGUAGES/MONACO_LANGUAGES, formatting.ts:30); VERSION_ALIASES (catalog.mjs:69) and KNOWN_UNAVAILABLE (catalog.mjs:119), both of which the client needs and lacks; runtimeNoteFor (catalog.mjs:319) — each switch arm is just a template over version fields, so a runtimeNote string per language does it; and a real `kind: program | preview | asset | data` to replace the unread runner.command sentinels. Indent size, comment syntax and entry-point naming patterns are the same story.

Genuinely functions, which force a code half: monaco-config.ts:118 pushing compiler options into monaco.languages.typescript.*; execution.ts:114 reading Monaco markers to gate a run; format-core.ts brace/indent algorithms; import-refactor.ts:914 per-language import rewriting; run-panel.ts:127 definition extraction; code-analysis.ts parsers. These take live Monaco/AST objects and return edits. No JSON encoding of them is honest.

So: a two-part registry. Data half stays in languages/<id>/config.json — extended with the flags above, shared with the server for free, and covering roughly 80% of today's hardcoded per-language lists. Behaviour half is a code-side adapter map keyed by language id. For the code half, prefer an explicit map with static imports over a glob — exactly server/languages/registry.mjs:22, whose whole point is stated in its header comment ("the point of this file is what is NOT in it"). That keeps adapters under src/ where tsconfig checks them against the contract, keeps lookup synchronous, and makes adding a language one import plus one map entry. Reserve import.meta.glob for what it is already good at: discovering data files that live next to their language.

Two more things a unified registry should reconcile. First, TWO KEYSPACES: language id and monacoLanguage are many-to-one (svg -> xml), and formatting.ts:51 hasFormatter() is keyed by monaco id while everything else is keyed by language id. The loader builds no reverse index, so any registry lookup from a live model needs one. Second, the client and server can DISAGREE: the client's view is frozen at build time by the glob, the server's is an fs read with a 5-minute TTL, and GET /api/languages exists but no client code calls it. Until a deploy, a config.json change is visible to the server and invisible to the client.

WHAT THE MODULE IS FOR. src/components/code-analysis.ts is a dependency-free, regex-and-heuristics source scanner with exactly two exports and one exported type. (2) `extractDefinitionsOnly(code, language): string` — the source text with top-level *executing* statements stripped, leaving only function/class definitions, so one function can be invoked in isolation without the file's main body running first. WHO CONSUMES IT. Exactly one importer in the whole repo: src/features/run-panel.ts:2 (verified by repo-wide grep excluding node_modules/dist; the only other hit is a one-line mention in src/README.md:16). `parseFunctions` is called at run-panel.ts:33 from `renderFunctionList`, which is re-run on every editor content change (debounced 500ms) and on every model/tab switch — so this regex work runs on the UI thread twice a second while typing, over the whole file, with `maskCommentsAndStrings` doing per-character string concatenation. There are NO unit tests: tests/unit contains a format-core.test.ts but nothing for code-analysis, so every regex here is unverified.

The IDE's real language set is the six config-driven languages in /languages/*/config.json (javascript, typescript, python, java, php, csharp) PLUS five BUILTIN_LANGUAGES registered in src/languages/loader.ts:33-104: html, css, svg, json, markdown. `normalizeLanguage` returns null for all five.
